newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber slips after setting new high in March.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber slips after setting new high in March.

text.p: CME lumber futures opened higher on carryover demand from Thursday's limit gains in January and March and set a new contract high in March before profit taking quickly turned most months lower, traders said.

March posted a new contract high of $410.00 per tbf and January rose to its highest level since December 10 before retreating. At 0922 CST, lumber stood $2.90 higher to $2.40 lower with only January up at $410.00 and March off $0.90 at $404.0 per tbf.
Further bull spreading kept January firm while weighing on deferreds, traders added.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $392 per tbf, up $9 from midweek and $6 under last Friday's level. Activity and demand increased midweek after being slow early in the week, they said.
